rubric.label: Wedge
rubric.question: Is the promise sharp enough to own a market sentence?

rubric.label: Portable Pi
rubric.question: Does it foreground local Pi skills, prompts, AGENTS.md, model defaults, and habits on a remote agent?

rubric.label: Browser Remote
rubric.question: Can someone understand Pi running from the browser against cloud sandboxes?

rubric.label: Recurring
rubric.question: Does it make repeat/standing agents feel natural?

rubric.label: Env Fit
rubric.question: Does it explain custom setup, env keys, install commands, and repo conventions?

rubric.label: Cloud Loop
rubric.question: Does it promise better remote iteration with guardrails, tests, reviewers, and stop conditions?

rubric.label: Proof
rubric.question: Does it end in reviewable evidence: diffs, logs, screenshots, reports, or PRs?

rubric.label: Shipping Truth
rubric.question: Can we say it without sounding fake or overclaiming current implementation?

rubric.label: Landing Clarity
rubric.question: Does the H1, hero visual, and CTA scan in under five seconds?

rounds.title: Round 0 - existing worktrees
rounds.prompt: Score the eight concepts already built as worktrees.
rounds.transition: The best concepts all make the remote agent feel personal. Browser-only is clear but not defensible; evidence is useful but not a wedge.
rounds.nextMove: Mutate toward portable Pi profile, browser launch, and reusable setup.

candidates.name: browser-pi
candidates.h1: Run Pi in the browser.
candidates.thesis: Broad browser-first pitch; strong clarity, weaker uniqueness.

candidates.name: bring-your-pi
candidates.h1: Your local Pi setup. On a remote agent.
candidates.thesis: Best uniqueness; directly addresses local Pi skills and habits on remote agents.

candidates.name: recurring-agents
candidates.h1: Make Pi come back tomorrow.
candidates.thesis: Strong retention idea; not enough Pi-specific differentiation.

candidates.name: env-capsules
candidates.h1: Remote agents that know your setup.
candidates.thesis: Excellent env/setup story; less emotional than local Pi portability.

candidates.name: cloud-loops
candidates.h1: Better loops for cloud agents.
candidates.thesis: Strong operating model; less singular as a landing headline.

candidates.name: setup-blueprint
candidates.h1: Teach the cloud your dev setup once.
candidates.thesis: Good onboarding promise; reads like a feature more than the product.

candidates.name: html-evidence
candidates.h1: Not HTML artifacts. Evidence.
candidates.thesis: Important proof layer; too narrow as the main page.

candidates.name: remote-roster
candidates.h1: A bench of remote Pi agents.
candidates.thesis: Good product shape; needs setup portability to feel novel.

rounds.title: Round 1 - portable setup mutations
rounds.prompt: Generate ten concepts from the top Round 0 genes: bring-your-pi, env-capsules, and setup-blueprint.
rounds.transition: Passport language wins because it carries identity, permissions, and portability. The weak spot remains recurring usefulness.
rounds.nextMove: Keep profile portability and add standing agents plus evidence output.

candidates.name: Pi Passport
candidates.h1: Give remote agents your Pi passport.
candidates.thesis: A profile bundle travels with each sandbox: skills, prompts, provider defaults, repo rules, and env recipe.

candidates.name: Cloud Clone
candidates.h1: Clone your Pi into the cloud.
candidates.thesis: High drama copy for syncing the local Pi experience into remote runners.

candidates.name: Setup Backpack
candidates.h1: Pack your setup once. Send it with every agent.
candidates.thesis: Setup is a portable backpack attached to each cloud run.

candidates.name: Browser Pi Plus Profile
candidates.h1: Run Pi in the browser, with your profile attached.
candidates.thesis: Combines broad browser comprehension with local Pi profile sync.

candidates.name: Skill Sync Sandbox
candidates.h1: Your skills in every remote sandbox.
candidates.thesis: Makes skills the hero rather than the broader Pi profile.

candidates.name: Standing Profile
candidates.h1: One profile for agents that come back.
candidates.thesis: Turns local Pi setup into the base layer for scheduled agents.

candidates.name: Personal Remote Runner
candidates.h1: Remote agents that run like your Pi.
candidates.thesis: Plain-spoken personal remote runner promise.

candidates.name: Dotfiles in the Cloud
candidates.h1: Your dotfiles, skills, and Pi in the cloud.
candidates.thesis: Too much dotfile overclaim, but names the local setup desire.

candidates.name: Cloud Workbench for Pi
candidates.h1: A cloud workbench for Pi agents.
candidates.thesis: Accurate but sounds category-generic.

candidates.name: Run Forever
candidates.h1: Turn any Pi prompt into a recurring cloud run.
candidates.thesis: Great recurrence angle; local Pi profile is secondary.

rounds.title: Round 2 - recurrence and proof graft
rounds.prompt: Generate ten concepts from Pi Passport, Personal Remote Runner, and Standing Profile.
rounds.transition: Personal Pi Cloud wins by making the product bigger than sync while preserving the local profile advantage.
rounds.nextMove: Sharpen the metaphor and add cloud-loop language without making the page abstract.

candidates.name: Personal Pi Cloud
candidates.h1: A personal cloud for your Pi agents.
candidates.thesis: A named cloud space where remote agents inherit your Pi profile, run on schedule, and return evidence.

candidates.name: Your Pi, On Schedule
candidates.h1: Put your Pi setup on a schedule.
candidates.thesis: Best for recurring jobs, but the browser/cloud story is quieter.

candidates.name: Cloud Agents With Your Pi DNA
candidates.h1: Cloud agents with your Pi DNA.
candidates.thesis: Memorable identity phrase; slightly gimmicky.

candidates.name: Pi Profile, Remote Runs
candidates.h1: Your Pi profile. Real remote runs.
candidates.thesis: Clear, shippable, and direct.

candidates.name: Remote Agent Memory
candidates.h1: Remote agents that remember your setup.
candidates.thesis: Good retention metaphor, weaker Pi specificity.

candidates.name: Clone Setup, Keep Control
candidates.h1: Clone the setup. Keep the review.
candidates.thesis: Balanced between setup and human-approved evidence.

candidates.name: Browser Runs, Local Taste
candidates.h1: Browser runs with local Pi taste.
candidates.thesis: High browser clarity, but the phrasing is too cute.

candidates.name: Approved Autopilot
candidates.h1: An autopilot that asks before it lands.
candidates.thesis: Strong cloud-loop guardrails; local setup underweighted.

candidates.name: Evidence First Pi Cloud
candidates.h1: Every remote Pi run leaves receipts.
candidates.thesis: Excellent proof layer, not the primary wedge.

candidates.name: One Profile, Many Agents
candidates.h1: One Pi profile. Many remote agents.
candidates.thesis: Simple product model, slightly less emotional.

rounds.title: Round 3 - metaphor and operating loop
rounds.prompt: Generate ten concepts from Personal Pi Cloud plus the best clear/truthful alternatives.
rounds.transition: Brain/hands language wins: it explains local cognition plus remote execution in one line.
rounds.nextMove: Translate the metaphor into landing copy that does not sound like sci-fi.

candidates.name: Your Pi Brain, Cloud Hands
candidates.h1: Your Pi brain. Cloud hands.
candidates.thesis: Your local Pi profile decides how work happens; remote sandboxes do the heavy lifting.

candidates.name: Pi That Leaves Your Laptop
candidates.h1: Pi that can leave your laptop.
candidates.thesis: Strong mental image for browser/remote access.

candidates.name: The Remote Agent That Knows You
candidates.h1: The remote agent that knows your Pi setup.
candidates.thesis: Clear promise, but softer than brain/hands.

candidates.name: Cloud Loops, Local Rules
candidates.h1: Cloud loops. Local Pi rules.
candidates.thesis: Excellent operating model for tests, reviewers, stop conditions, and setup.

candidates.name: Bring the Whole Pi Rig
candidates.h1: Bring the whole Pi rig.
candidates.thesis: Good for power users, less clear to new visitors.

candidates.name: Schedule Your Pi Clone
candidates.h1: Schedule your Pi clone.
candidates.thesis: High recurrence, but clone language overpromises.

candidates.name: One Click Remote Pi
candidates.h1: One click to a remote Pi run.
candidates.thesis: Great conversion clarity, not enough defensibility.

candidates.name: Pi Cloud With Receipts
candidates.h1: A Pi cloud with receipts.
candidates.thesis: Makes evidence memorable and useful.

candidates.name: Private Pi Profile Cloud
candidates.h1: A private cloud for your Pi profile.
candidates.thesis: Good trust posture, less action-oriented.

candidates.name: Remote Workers For Your Pi
candidates.h1: Remote workers for your Pi.
candidates.thesis: Plain but risks sounding like generic worker infrastructure.

rounds.title: Round 4 - landing headline stress test
rounds.prompt: Generate ten landing-ready headlines from the best Round 3 concepts.
rounds.transition: Follows-you language beats brain/hands because it is warmer, clearer, and still implies portability.
rounds.nextMove: Finalize around the follows-you headline and verify it can carry the proof sections.

candidates.name: Teach the cloud your Pi once

candidates.name: Your Pi setup, rented remote hands

candidates.name: Pi cloud runs with a paper trail

candidates.name: Recurring fixes from a cloud Pi

rounds.title: Round 5 - final ten
rounds.prompt: Generate ten final candidates from the winning headline and stress them against truth, proof, and conversion clarity.
rounds.transition: The final winner keeps the warm follows-you H1, then lets browser, recurring agents, env capsules, cloud loops, and evidence act as proof.
rounds.nextMove: Implement a landing page around the winner.
